title: H₀ ∘ C_• ⊣ Loc_φ adjunction (§3 Prop)
body_html:
Adjunction $H_0 \circ C_\bullet \;\dashv\; \Loc_\phi$

Proposition. The functor $\Loc_\phi : \Rep_\phi(G) \to \Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)$ is a right adjoint of $H_0 \circ C_\bullet : \Cosh_G(X, R, \phi) \to \Rep_\phi(G)$.

Counit

For $V \in \Rep_\phi(G)$, the augmentation $\epsilon_V : C_0(\Loc_\phi V) \to V$ (see [[node:representations.chain_complex_C_dot]]) kills boundaries and factors through $H_0$ because $V = \sum_x V[\phi_x]$ by assumption. This gives $$\epsilon_V : H_0(C_\bullet(\Loc_\phi V)) \to V.$$

Unit

For $\mathscr{V} \in \Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)$ and a cell $E$, set $$(\eta_\mathscr{V})_E := q_\mathscr{V} \circ r^\mathscr{V}_{E, x}$$ for any vertex $x \in \overline E$, where $q_\mathscr{V} : C_0(\mathscr{V}) \twoheadrightarrow H_0(C_\bullet \mathscr{V})$ is the canonical quotient. The composite is independent of the choice of $x$ by the definition of $H_0$. Its image lies in $H_0(C_\bullet \mathscr{V})[\phi_E]$ because $q_\mathscr{V} \circ r^\mathscr{V}_{E, x}$ is $K_E$-equivariant. This gives $\eta : \mathrm{id} \to \Loc_\phi \circ H_0 \circ C_\bullet$.

Unit–counit identities

  • For $V \in \Rep_\phi(G)$: $\Loc_\phi(\epsilon_V) \circ \eta_{\Loc_\phi V} = \id_{\Loc_\phi V}$. On each cell $E$, $v \in V[\phi_E]$ maps to $q(r^{\Loc_\phi V}_{E, x}(v))$, then to $r^{\Loc_\phi V}_{E,x}(v)$ under $\epsilon_V$; composing with the projection back to $V[\phi_E]$ is the identity since $r^{\Loc_\phi V}_{E,x}$ is just inclusion.
  • For $\mathscr{V} \in \Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)$: $\epsilon_{H_0 C_\bullet \mathscr{V}} \circ H_0(C_\bullet \eta_\mathscr{V}) = \id_{H_0 C_\bullet \mathscr{V}}$. Direct computation on $z = \sum_x x \otimes v_x$ tracks the identity. $\square$

A standard corollary (Cosh_G(X,R,φ)[Σ⁻¹] ≃ Rep_φ(G) (§3 Cor)): if the counit is an isomorphism for every $V$, then $H_0 \circ C_\bullet$ exhibits $\Rep_\phi(G)$ as a localization of $\Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)$ at the class of morphisms inducing $H_0$-isomorphisms.
